title: Keyboard-first Quickflows: remote moderated usability & wireframe critique
content:
Summary:

Short remote moderated usability run focused on keyboard-first interactions for the Quickflows wireframe (v2). Goal: validate whether keyboard shortcuts, focus order, and small inline affordances let power users complete three core flows without falling back to the mouse. This doc is a working synthesis (notes + raw quotes) and a groomed backlog of suggested small-ticket fixes we should prioritize for the next sprint.

Test setup:
- Modality: remote moderated (Zoom + screen share), 6 participants (mix of ML engineers, infra/platform engineers, and dev-ex from partners)
- Prototype: Figma clickable wireframe + short sandbox token generator (mock api)
- Timebox: 45 minutes per session (10m intro, 25m tasks, 10m debrief)
- Success metrics: task completion (no mouse), time-on-task, number of accidental tab traps, subjective ease (1-5)

Participants (high level):
- P1: ML infra eng, heavy keyboard user
- P2: Platform eng, occasional mouse
- P3: Solutions eng, uses shortcuts heavily
- P4: Security reviewer, accessibility-conscious
- P5: Senior FE eng, power user
- P6: Customer success SME, mixed habits

Tasks given (explicit):
1) Create a new Quickflow from template, change model variant, and save as team draft (without using mouse).
2) Re-run a recent job with different runtime profile and attach a note to the run (keyboard-only).
3) Locate rollout controls in the console, start a canary rollout, and switch to fallback (keyboard-only).

High-level findings:
- Core hypothesis validated: keyboard-first flows are feasible for power users, but only if focus order and visible shortcuts are consistent across microcomponents.
- Biggest blocker: inconsistent tabindex/focus traps in the inline editable table and the model-select modal. 4/6 participants hit tab traps and had to use mouse to recover.
- Discoverability: users expect a persistent keyboard help overlay (press ? to open) anchored to top-right — several asked for it.
- Inline actions (three-dot menus) are not reachable by keyboard when activated via Enter on row; focus is not routed to menu items.
- Modal focus: when opening the model variant modal, focus lands on the modal background container instead of the first actionable control.
- Feedback affordance: undo / toast actions (e.g., "Saved draft") are not keyboard-focusable which blocks keyboard recovery after an accidental save.

Representative quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "I rely on tabbing through tables — once I hit that control it just...stops." (P1)
- "I expected pressing space on the row to open the menu, but focus just stayed on the row text." (P3)
- "A small help overlay with shortcuts would be huge — I can't remember 12 combos." (P5)

Wireframe-specific notes (issues + quick visual suggestions):
- Model-select modal: move primary action to first tabbable element; ensure role=dialog and aria-modal are set in implementation. (low-fi note: add visible keyboard hint above dropdown)
- Inline table: change row-level button pattern to a focusable action column with visible shortcut tooltip on focus. (sketch: small column with keyboard icon)
- Three-dot menu: on open, set focus to first menu item and support ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation; escape returns focus to originating control.
- Toasts: make toasts keyboard-focusable and provide "dismiss" action reachable via keyboard; announce to screen readers when an undo is available.
- Persistent shortcuts overlay: wireframe a small ? button in top-right that opens a dismissible panel with contextual shortcuts per route.

Prioritized backlog (small tickets for sprint 139):
- PRJ-3012: Fix tab trap in quickflows table rows (estimate 2 dev days) — critical.
- PRJ-3013: Model variant modal focus order + aria attrs (1 dev day) — high.
- PRJ-3014: Keyboard-accessible toast/undo component (1.5 days) — medium.
- PRJ-3015: Global shortcuts overlay (spec + wireframe) (2 days design + 1 day FE scaffolding) — medium.
- PRJ-3016: Add visible shortcut hints in action column (design + small CSS) — low.

Acceptance criteria (for top 2 tickets):
- PRJ-3012: All table rows can be fully navigated and operated using keyboard only (tab, shift+tab, enter, space, arrow keys where applicable). No session required to use mouse. Unit tests for tabindex and e2e test reproducing previous trap.
- PRJ-3013: Opening model variant modal moves focus to dropdown; aria-modal present; screen reader announces dialog name. E2E verifies focus landing and escape behavior.

Metrics to track post-fix (proposal):
- % tasks completed without mouse (pre/post compare)
- Tab-trap incidents per session (instrumented error logs or automated e2e checks)
- Time-on-task change for the 3 core flows
- Support tickets referencing "can't tab" or "keyboard" in console search (monthly)

Quick implementation notes for infra/FE team:
- Small CSS change to focus outline will improve visibility of active element across themes (dark/light).
- Use a11y-testing tool (axe) in CI for regression on tabindex and role issues.
- Add a lightweight keyboard telemetry flag for experimental rollout to 5% of accounts to measure adoption.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should Quickflows provide two modes (beginner vs power) with different default shortcut sets? Pros/cons needed from product.
- Do we want to expose user-customizable shortcuts in console MVP? (scope decision)
- Confirm analytics: what signal will we accept as "keyboard success" for GA? (ops + analytics input needed)

Next steps:
1) Groom PRJ-3012 and PRJ-3013 into sprint 139 backlog; assign to FE lead.
2) Design to wire a lightweight shortcuts overlay and microcopy for toasts (Evelyn).
3) FE/infra to add basic axe checks + e2e that runs a keyboard flow smoke test.
4) Re-run a 4-user rapid remote check after fixes (2 weeks) to validate improvements.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally rough — contains verbatim snippets and quick designs. Please comment inline in the figma link for any visual suggestions; for product decisions add comments to JIRA-1287.
